messages.subject: Overplotting data from different files
parts:

The files has contents as follows

-----------------------
"deltat" "deltam2" "deltam2err" "deltam"
"0.000231" "0.00852003" "0.00556962" "0.092304"

"0.000232" "0.0015224" "0.00235122" "0.039018"
"0.000233" "0.141117" "0.157653" "-0.375656"
------------------------

file2:
-------------------------------
"deltat" "deltam2" "deltam2err" "deltam"
"0.000232" "0.00834464" "0.0417891" "0.091349"
"0.000232" "0.235443" "0.267455" "0.485225"
"0.000232" "0.827569" "0.726109" "0.909708"
"0.000235" "0.609127" "0.690786" "-0.780466"
"0.000236" "0.00619511" "0.0351618" "-0.078709"
"0.000239" "0.000336099" "0.00423375" "-0.018333"
"0.000239" "0.00255197" "0.0117231" "0.050517"
"0.00024" "0.00252155" "0.0230554" "-0.050215"
"0.000243" "0.0725618" "0.063245" "-0.269373"
---------------------------------

While both file has same number of columns, each has different no. of rows.

I want to over-plot like following,  say

ggplot(file1,aes(deltat,deltam) + ggplot(file2,aes(deltat,deltam).

How is it possible? Please help.


Thanks in advance.

Noble

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Overplotting data from different files
parts:
Dear Noble,

That is possible. But not by using ggplot() twice. Soppuse you want to
display the first file as points. Then the code would be


ggplot(file1,aes(deltat,deltam)) + geom_point()

If you want to add the second file as an extra layer of points then the
code would be

ggplot(file1,aes(deltat,deltam)) + geom_point() + geom_point(data =
file2)

So the trick is to add the extra geoms that you need and supply the new
dataframe with the data argument. Note that you can also change the
aesthetics if the names in the new dataframe are different.

ggplot(file1,aes(x = deltat, y = deltam)) + geom_point() +
geom_point(data = file2, aes(x = deltam, y = deltat))

Best regards,

Thierry

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: RE: Overplotting data from different files
parts:
Dear Noble,
 
A better solution would be to merge all the files into a single dataframe.
 
file1$Filename <- "File 1"
file2$Filename <- "File 2"
file3$Filename <- "File 3"
Union <- rbind(file1, file2, file3)
ggplot(Union, aes(x = deltat, y = deltam, colour = Filename)) + geom_point()
 
Like that you will get a nice legend as well.
 
Best regards,
 
Thierry

messages.subject: Re: RE: Overplotting data from different files

On Thu, Jan 13, 2011 at 11:23 AM, Noble P Abraham <nob...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thank you Thierry,
>
> That looks fine. but if want to use N files to be plotted, can a loop be
> made?
>

You can, yes (see solution 2 below), but it's more likely that you'll
rather want to combine the data beforehand.


## fake data sets organised in a list
my.data <- replicate(5,data.frame(x=1:10,y=rnorm(10)),simplify=FALSE)

names(my.data) <- paste("file",seq_along(my.data))
str(my.data)

## version 1, combine data.frames

m <- melt(my.data,id='x')
str(m)

ggplot(m) +
geom_path(aes(x,value,colour=L1))

## version 2, using a loop to add layers

make.layer <- function(ii){
geom_path(aes(x,y), data=my.data[[ii]], colour=ii)
}
all.layers <- llply(seq(2,length(my.data)), make.layer)

p.ini <- ggplot(my.data[[1]]) +
geom_path(aes(x,y))

p.ini + all.layers

HTH,

baptiste
